CH2008-WIN.evidence: Chase et al. Table 1 and sections 2–4. Correlated offset drives show an 86 cm package in a 3.9 m deep cirque lake with shore-side avalanche tracks. Stratigraphic attribution and good local recovery do not quantify upslope or underwater focusing.

CH2008-THU.evidence: Chase et al. Table 1 and section 4.2. The two contacts enclose 32 cm in gyttja. Authors describe poor correlation of parallel drives above the marker in this 2.9 m deep lake.

M2024-ROUNDWA.evidence: Mark thesis section 5.3.1, Fig. 46. The approximately 606–666 cm event package lies within carbonate-rich sediment. No quantified primary fraction, catchment input or focusing correction supports a minimum of 60 cm.

B2020-113.evidence: Buckland S1 row 125 reports two layers. Mehringer in Johnson et al. (1994) p. 6 and his Columbia River Basin account describe two horizons separated by 9 cm of lake sediment. The 46 cm cannot be assigned to one climactic bed, or shown to enclose the complete deposit of that eruption.

B2020-073.evidence: Buckland et al. report 30 cm of continuous fine tephra over a sharp contact below developed soil at Andies Prairie. Their field visit and S2 watershed-divide analysis support their explicit minimum interpretation.

B2020-038.evidence: S1 gives 68 cm as an upland thickness. The original field log, scope of phases and physical basis of the upland value could not be independently tied to this exposure. Young’s separately numbered mapped sections retain their own evidence.

B2020-049.evidence: Buckland S1 gives 37 cm. The four-lake study abstract does not identify this value by lake, and the recovered investigator archive entry is a modern surface sample. Neither verifies complete recovery of this tephra at the nominated site.

B2020-059.evidence: The investigator archive identifies the Mazama depth control but quotes a 1 cm dating sample and a different depth from S1. The 17 cm S1 value cannot be aligned to a confirmed original bed and bounded recovery.

B2020-177.evidence: S1 gives a varying 15 cm for the Maple Leaf site. Jensen et al. Table S1 reports a 15 cm observation at Stampede (UA 2825), a separate site, and contains no entry for Maple Leaf. The original excavation profile assigning 15 cm to one intact blanket is unresolved.

B2020-149.evidence: The Mack study and the corrected Tepee Lake location support an occurrence. Neither the accessible original account nor Kuehn’s separate Glacier Peak sample establishes a 10 cm climactic bed, its contacts or retention.

B2020-121.evidence: S1 reports 5 cm at Creston/Wilbur Bog. Its relation to Creston Bog (S1 120) and to differently reported corrected and uncorrected values is unresolved. An exact section and original preserved bed were not identified.

B2020-227.evidence: Hallett et al. dated charcoal within the Dog Lake ash. The 10 cm compilation value and the 23 cm Dog Lake unit cited by Jensen Table S1 row 62 cannot presently be assigned to one particular core and transfer. Both readings remain in the ledger.

B2020-042.evidence: Larsen et al. 2016 Tables 1–3 and 2024 Fig. 3/section 4.1 confirm an airfall marker across Jenny Lake. The S1 1 cm at the JEN13-1C coordinate is not verified as a member-specific thickness; the analyzed sample is from JEN13-2E. A sampled interval and near-delta turbidites do not provide that bed measurement.

B2020-122.evidence: The historical wet 15–30 cm at Newman Lake and the 22.5 cm compilation midpoint do not locate both endpoints at a single recoverable core footprint or control lake focusing. Either gain or loss is possible; neither endpoint supplies a defensible sign.

B2020-017.evidence: Bovet et al. confirm coring and the ash/date marker, and S1 describes the recovered package as 2–6 cm. Use the largest reported bed to allow local focusing, conditional on the compiled range applying to this lake and on complete capture.

B2020-019.evidence: Bovet et al. identify a cored eastern subbasin after abandoning the deep basin. The S1 2–6 cm range is not an independent field measurement. The 6 cm upper endpoint allows focusing under the qualified core and retention assignment.

B2020-063.evidence: Young Table 1.1 and Fig. 1.14 identify a field-checked bog locality and standardize the loading to 700 kg/m³. Halving the standardized thickness accounts for a proposed bulk-density ratio but does not bound lateral import, wet-to-dry volume change or older ash. Observer values and Young’s estimate remain a common alternative.

B2020-068.evidence: Young Table 1.1 and Fig. 1.14 identify a field-checked bog locality and standardize the loading to 700 kg/m³. Halving the standardized thickness accounts for a proposed bulk-density ratio but does not bound lateral import, wet-to-dry volume change or older ash. Observer values and Young’s estimate remain a common alternative.

B2020-076.evidence: Young Table 1.1 and Fig. 1.14 identify a field-checked bog locality and standardize the loading to 700 kg/m³. Halving the standardized thickness accounts for a proposed bulk-density ratio but does not bound lateral import, wet-to-dry volume change or older ash. Observer values and Young’s estimate remain a common alternative.

B2020-023.evidence: The 5 cm tephra V is independently measured and compositionally distinguished from tephra VI. The investigators specifically discuss rapid settling and possible subaqueous flow in connection with its unusual magnetic direction. The logged deposit may exceed local fallout.

B2020-099.evidence: The Buckland extraction gives both contacts, 7.21–7.27 m, and the independent dating crosswalk brackets Mazama at Davis Lake. The 6 cm is a recovered-host ceiling conditional on the inherited depths and continuity; it is not a separately verified primary blanket measurement.

B2020-126.evidence: The investigator’s report differentiates a near-margin debris-flow occurrence from other Leland cores, and verifies Mazama by microprobe. The section at which the compiled 2 cm was measured has not been matched to its geochemistry and depositional state.

B2020-174.evidence: The Squeah nearshore core has correlated ash and an underlying radiocarbon sample (I-5347). The site-specific source thickness and completeness of the S1 2 cm package at this position remain unresolved.

B2020-160.evidence: Several Lulu Island holes and X-ray emission analyses support eruption identity. The compilation does not identify the exact borehole and contacts associated with 1.5 cm or whether it is a whole bed.

B2020-148.evidence: S1 explicitly distinguishes an 8 cm earlier fall and 12 cm climactic unit. Valastro et al. establish two intervals in the fen. A 12 cm ceiling allows concentration in the later peat bed; it is conditional on the source assigning that complete reported unit to this hole.

B2020-291.evidence: The historic corer recorded a 1 mm layer and Young Table 1.1 gives an upper equivalent of 0.2 cm at 700 kg/m³. Jensen S1 row 57 corroborates that an identifiable visible Mazama horizon was reported. Use Young’s stated ceiling, conditional on the density and source recovery; no calibrated zero or detection threshold.

M2014-CLELAND-F.evidence: Mihindukulasooriya’s F-09 ash interval is 4 or 5 cm in the primary accounts. Use the larger complete-bed endpoint to allow concentration. Carbonate-rich material in the different E-09 core cannot independently measure primary thickness at F-09.

W1995-TT06313.evidence: The original workshop account reports an identified discrete offshore ash at 209–211 cm. Whether those limits are whole physical contacts or the sampled slice cannot be resolved. Sea-floor transport and export can change the loading in either direction.

ROS2004-EAG.evidence: Rosenberg et al. Tables 2 and 4 support the eruption identity, including glass chemistry, and a 15 cm core package (81–96 cm). Central-basin accumulation is not independently compared with a local atmospheric blanket.

ROS2004-FRO.evidence: Rosenberg et al. Table 2 separates the 155–163 cm lake package from other units. Its full 8 cm supports a conditional retention ceiling. No independently separated primary thickness is reported.

P1999-BEAVER-OR.evidence: The thesis and published chronology place the complete 2 cm Beaver Lake interval at different composite depths. A common 2 cm package in the lake can allow lateral addition without imposing a positive original minimum.

MK2012-PATJENS.evidence: McKay describes a 4 cm silicic bed in a short south-shore fen core. The correlation is presumed from stratigraphy and grain size. The whole bed could have been augmented in this setting.

W2017-LSUNRISE.evidence: Coring ended within the tephra after 3 cm. It is a firm lower limit on recovered lake material. The missing lower contact prevents a full-package ceiling, and the investigators do not calibrate focusing at the coring position.

R2021-LONG.evidence: Rushton et al. report approximately 7 cm in the LOL14C eastern Cascades composite. Composite-depth and chronology discrepancies and unquantified focusing weaken a point reading; the entire package gives a conditional ceiling.

B2020-203.evidence: Mathewes describes a discrete 3.5 cm glass-bearing layer with stratigraphic age support at Surprise Lake. Only the complete lake bed is measured; use a retention-conditional ceiling.

B2020-251.evidence: Mathewes describes 5 cm in Marion Lake. The deep coring position and rapid flushing leave focusing unresolved. Interpret the complete bed as a retention-conditional ceiling.

B2020-205.evidence: Lowdon and Blake GSC-1004 describe a 10 cm peat-contained ash and query the Mazama assignment. The complete logged bed allows a conditional ceiling if the correlation holds.

B2020-169.evidence: Lowdon and Blake GSC-875 separate an 8 cm lower peat bed from a 3 cm upper ash. The climactic correlation of the lower bed is taken from later work. Compression and archives of imported ash remain uncertain.

MAR2009-S15.evidence: Marcott’s creek section places tephra immediately over till and below sand. The mapped 50–66 cm recovered thickness is an outward interval read from the section; fluvial or glacial concentration cannot be excluded at this position. Keep the upper endpoint under full retention.

MAR2009-S05.evidence: The upstream cutbank contains separated ash-bearing bands and outwash. The 4–9 cm graphical estimate for one band neither isolates an unaffected primary basal fallout layer nor encloses all possible target material.

B2020-275.evidence: Jensen et al. Table S1 row 27, UA 2901. The fresh road-cut section has a sharp base and a reworked top; the whole layer varies from 2 to 5 cm. Use 5 cm as a conditional ceiling at the reported field coordinate. The 2–3 cm typical thickness contains an unresolved secondary share.

B2020-285.evidence: Jensen et al. Table S1 row 50, UA 2979, reports a questioned upper thickness of 1 cm in Hasse Lake, with glass analyzed. The 253–266 cm field entry is a core-depth range. S1 warns of distortion. Accept the author’s tentative upper only if recovery is complete.

R2001-KSNEA.evidence: Riedel, Pringle and Schuster separate an abrupt 2 cm basal airfall above pre-eruption lake sediment from as much as 17 m of reworked delta. Pringle and Scott corroborate this measured component as co-author testimony. The point represents the delta near the creek mouth.

L2012-ROE.evidence: Fig. 2 resolves the ash between 573.0 and 573.5 cm. The photographed discrete layer, composition and depositional setting support a 0.5 cm preserved primary bed.

L2016-STOWELL.evidence: Lemmen logs a 2 cm bed at 330.5–332.5 cm in organic sediment. Stratigraphic age and regional chemistry comparisons support a likely Mazama attribution.

M2013-NEL01.evidence: Six centimetres in one lacustrine core. The original author correlates the bed to the climactic eruption using the stratigraphic age model.

M2013-NEL03.evidence: Tables 2.2 and 3.1 imply 27 and 26 cm for the lower airfall bed. The separate upper redeposit is 6.5–8.5 cm and contains weathered clay. The small basin has an inlet; take the wider primary package as a conditional ceiling.

M2012-ONOFF02.evidence: Fig. 5, PDF p. 6 (printed p. 76), core 02. Continuous Unit 2 encloses the 141 cm glass signal. Axis ticks 0/150 cm at y=202/563; outward contact picks 405/601 pixels at 1042×1389 yield 81.44 cm rounded outward to 82. The whole host unit is deliberately broad.

N2004-CASTOR.evidence: Nelson describes rapid deposition of about 30 cm of ash and later continuing surface wash. Only the initial package supplies an approximate conditional upper bound.

E1997-A12.evidence: Fig. 4.2, PDF p. 77 / printed p. 65, longest complete central core A12. At a rendering 870 pixels wide, 240 cm spans y=135–606 in its log. Outward ash edges at y=513–520 span 3.57 cm, rounded upward to 4 cm. Section L3/L4 in Table 5.1. Appendix 4 zone spans are sediment-yield bins and may differ from the visual ash contacts.

E1997-B7B.evidence: Fig. 4.2, PDF p. 77 / printed p. 65, longest complete central core B7b. At a rendering 870 pixels wide, 240 cm spans y=135–616 in its log. Outward ash edges at y=233–273 span 19.96 cm, rounded upward to 20 cm. Section P2/P3 in Table 5.1. Appendix 4 zone spans are sediment-yield bins and may differ from the visual ash contacts.

E1997-C5.evidence: Fig. 4.2, PDF p. 77 / printed p. 65, longest complete central core C5. At a rendering 870 pixels wide, 240 cm spans y=138–622 in its log. Outward ash edges at y=412–438 span 12.89 cm, rounded upward to 13 cm. Section G3/G4 in Table 5.1. Appendix 4 zone spans are sediment-yield bins and may differ from the visual ash contacts.

E1997-D8.evidence: Fig. 4.2, PDF p. 77 / printed p. 65, longest complete central core D8. At a rendering 870 pixels wide, 240 cm spans y=143–625 in its log. Outward ash edges at y=338–394 span 27.88 cm, rounded upward to 28 cm. Section Q2/Q3 in Table 5.1. Appendix 4 zone spans are sediment-yield bins and may differ from the visual ash contacts.
